subject: Factors and interactions in a glm

messages.author: eebd145ee721905a
messages.subject: Factors and interactions in a glm
parts:
I’m learning Nimble and I am trying to replicate a model fit from R's glm, but my estimated parameters do not match (see parameter estimates further below).  I wonder if this is because I am handling factor variables (and their interactions) incorrectly in Nimble or if it is related to some parameters not mixing well in my Nimble model. 

Questions: Is the discrepancy in estimated effects due to an incorrect model representation in Nimble or poor mixing in the MCMC chains?  More generally, how do I absorb one level of a factor into the intercept in Nimble?  Did I correctly code the interaction between age and gender?

Thanks for any guidance on this! Also please point me to any existing documentation that addresses these questions.

Brian



GLM: 
fit~glm(wearing_mask~gender_factor + age_factor + gender_factor:age_factor,
            data=mydataWOna,family=binomial())

Nimble code:
maskCode4_0 <- nimbleCode({
  ### Priors
  intercept~dnorm(0,sd=1000) 
  maleEffect~dnorm(0,sd = 1000)
  
  for(i in 1:4) {
    # Priors for age effect and age:male interaction
    if(i==1){
      ageEffect[i] <-0 # attempt to force 1st level of factor into intercept
      ageMaleI[i] <-0 # attempt to force 1st level of factor into intercept
    } else {
      ageEffect[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
      ageMaleI[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
    }
  }
  
  ### logit link and Bernoulli data probabilities
  for(i in 1:N) {
    logit(mask_prob[i]) <- intercept + maleEffect*male[i] + 
      ageClassBase[i]*ageEffect[ageClass[i]] + male[i]*ageMaleI[ageClass[i]]
    mask[i] ~ dbern(mask_prob[i])                  
  }
  
})

maskConsts <- list(N = dim(mydataWOna)[1],
                   ageClassBase=ifelse(as.integer(mydataWOna$age_factor)>1,1,0),
                   ageClass=as.integer(mydataWOna$age_factor),
                   male=as.integer(mydataWOna$gender_factor)-1
)
maskData <- list(mask = mydataWOna$wearing_mask)
maskInits <- list(intercept = 0.5, maleEffect = 0.1,ageEffect=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3),
                  ageMaleI=c(0,0,0,0))


mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(code = maskCode4_0, data = maskData, inits = maskInits,
                       monitors = c("intercept", "maleEffect",
                                    "ageEffect","ageMaleI"), 
                       thin = 100,
                       niter = 2000000, nburnin=10000,
                       nchains = 4, setSeed = FALSE,
                       constants = maskConsts,samplesAsCodaMCMC=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Factors and interactions in a glm
parts:
Hi Brian,

Use of 'if' in model code is only for defining different models from one piece of code, not for defining logic of a single model.

You'd want to do something like this:

ageEffect[1] <- 0
ageMale[1] <- 0
 for(i in 2:4) {
# Priors for age effect and age:male interaction

ageEffect[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
      ageMaleI[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
  }

What is happening right now is that presuming there is not an "i" that is set to 1 in your R global environment, the model is being defined with priors for i = 1,2,3,4 and not setting the values for the first element to be 0.

I didn't look any more closely at your code or results than just noticing that one issue. If after making the fix above, things still seem strange, feel free to write back.

Chris
